kind.en: IB Diploma · World Studies Extended Essay

title.en: Aligning Narratives to State Interests: Deciphering State-Driven Censorship in the Portrayal of China's Zero-Covid Policy on Online News Articles

question.en: To what extent did censorship legislation, particularly the Provisions for the Administration of Internet News Information Service, ensure language used in portraying China's Zero-Covid policy on online news articles aligned with China's state interests?

summary.en: An interdisciplinary study combining English Language & Literature with Global Politics. It applies Fairclough's three-dimensional critical discourse analysis to English-language articles from China Daily and Xinhua, reads them through postcolonial theory, and compares China's internet news regulations with Singapore's POFMA using Mill's method of difference.

value.en: Critical discourse analysis · Postcolonial theory · Comparative politics
